name: PointStack Accessibility for WooCommerce
author: vdelafuente

sections.description:
Since 28 June 2025 the European Accessibility Act (EAA) covers online shops that sell to consumers in the EU. Its technical target is WCAG 2.1 Level AA (through EN 301 549).

PointStack Accessibility checks the pages your customers buy through, repairs the markup your theme and plugins produce at the earliest layer that owns it, and tells you which component produced each problem. It adds no toolbar or widget for visitors: the fixes are in the page itself.

What it does

  • Scans the pages customers buy through – home, shop, product, cart, checkout and account pages, plus WooCommerce emails and the PDFs you link to. Cart and checkout are scanned with a sample product in a throw-away cart (nothing is saved, no order is created).
  • Fixes issues at the source – more than 35 reversible fixes, applied through WordPress and WooCommerce hooks first and a careful attribute-only output pass second. Every fix is a toggle with an undo.
  • Culprit detection – every issue says which theme, plugin, template override, block, shortcode or post produced the markup (for example “Theme: your theme — override of cart/cart.php”), whether PointStack Accessibility can fix it, a theme update would, or only the author can — with a one-click bug report to send them.
  • Regression guard – after any theme, plugin, WordPress or WooCommerce update the buying journey is re-scanned automatically and you’re alerted only about new issues: “After updating Example Payments 4.2 → 4.3: 3 new issues on checkout.” It also tells you when a fix stopped applying.
  • Browser check – a second pass in your own browser with axe-core finds what server-side checks can’t: colour contrast after CSS, focus visibility, focus hidden behind sticky bars, small touch targets, reflow at 320 px, cookie banners you can’t operate by keyboard.
  • Live accessibility statement – generated from scan data and kept up to date: known limitations in plain language, workarounds and target dates, accessibility features, how you test, contact details, and a dated version history. Changes wait for your approval by default.
  • Barrier report inbox – an accessible “report a problem” form for visitors (no CAPTCHA) with an admin inbox, replies by email and response tracking.
  • Manual checklist – guided keyboard and screen-reader steps through a full purchase, logged as evidence. Automated tools find roughly a third of WCAG problems; this covers the rest.
  • Content tools – alt-text manager with “mark decorative”, heading repair, pre-publish accessibility check in the block editor, readability scores (English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Dutch), optional AI alt-text suggestions through the WordPress AI Client (WordPress 7.0+).
  • EAA paperwork – microenterprise self-declaration and disproportionate-burden assessment templates (Annex VI).
  • Accessible HTML invoices – a semantic, printable alternative to untagged PDF invoices.

WooCommerce fixes include

Unique add-to-cart names, star ratings with text, required fields announced, live notices, correct autocomplete tokens, keyboard-operable variation swatches, labelled cart and order tables, a sort dropdown that doesn’t jump on change, checkout errors that move focus and link to their fields, add-to-cart and cart updates announced, visible focus on payment methods, an accessible product gallery.

Honest limits

No tool can make a site compliant on its own, and PointStack Accessibility never claims to. It finds and fixes a large share of common barriers, documents the rest, and gives you the evidence trail regulators and customers expect.

PointStack Accessibility Pro

  • Pro – full-site and scheduled scans, history and trends, before/after per page, evidence pack export (HTML/PDF, CSV, JSON), regression alerts by email, Slack and webhook, email support for bugs.
  • Studio (10 sites) – white-label reports and a shareable client dashboard.
  • Agency (50 sites) – multisite network view, REST API and WP-CLI (scan staging in CI before you deploy).

Every paid plan comes with a 5-day free trial. A card is needed to start it, and you are not charged if you cancel during the trial. Paid plans have a 14-day money-back guarantee if the plugin has a problem that makes it unusable and we cannot fix it. A licence covers the software, updates and email support for bugs in the plugin; it does not guarantee that your store complies with the European Accessibility Act or any other law, and it is not legal advice.

Plans and pricing

External services

This plugin can connect to the following services, only when you configure them:

  • The AI provider connected in WordPress (optional AI alt-text suggestions, WordPress 7.0+): when you click “Suggest”, the plugin uses the WordPress AI Client to send the image (medium size) and the page or product title to the provider the site owner connected in Settings → Connectors. That provider’s terms of use and privacy policy apply. The plugin stores no AI keys of its own.
  • Freemius (Freemius, Inc., licensing and checkout service): only if you accept the opt-in shown after activation (you can skip it), Freemius receives the site URL, WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, the admin’s name and email, and activation and deactivation events. If you buy a paid plan, checkout, licence activation and update checks also go through Freemius. Terms of service: https://freemius.com/terms/ — Privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Source code and libraries

All plugin JavaScript and CSS ships uncompressed and readable. One third-party library is bundled minified, as published by its authors:

  • axe-core 4.14.0 (assets/vendor/axe.min.js), MPL-2.0, used only by the browser check in the admin. Source: https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core
  • Freemius WordPress SDK (vendor/freemius), GPL, licensing and optional opt-in. Source: https://github.com/Freemius/wordpress-sdk
sections.installation:
Requirements: WordPress 6.9 or later, WooCommerce 8.5 or later and PHP 7.4 or later. Tested with WordPress 7.1, WooCommerce 11.2 and PHP 8.3.

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Accessibility → Overview and press Scan my store.
  3. Review the fixes under Accessibility → Fixes (sensible defaults are already on).
  4. Create your accessibility statement under Accessibility → Statement.
sections.faq:
Is this an overlay or widget?

No. Nothing is added for visitors to click. PointStack Accessibility changes the HTML your site sends (attributes, labels, roles) and adds a few lines of CSS and a small script for things only JavaScript can fix, such as announcing “added to cart”.

Will it make my store EAA compliant?

It will get you much closer and give you the documentation, but compliance also needs manual testing and sometimes changes only a developer can make. PointStack Accessibility tells you which ones and who to ask.

Is this legal advice? Does it guarantee compliance?

No. PointStack Accessibility is a working tool: it finds, fixes and documents barriers, and the statement and evidence pack record what you did. It does not certify or guarantee compliance with the European Accessibility Act or any other law, and automated checks cover only part of WCAG. You publish the accessibility statement as your own. For legal questions, ask a qualified adviser.

A fix changed something on my site. How do I undo it?

Go to Accessibility → Fixes and switch that fix off; the change disappears on the next page load and known page caches are purged. “Turn all off (undo)” switches every fix off at once. New installs start with fixes visible to administrators only, so you can check your shop, cart and checkout before customers see them (Settings → Scanning → Who sees fixes).

The scanner flags something my theme or another plugin produces

Open the issue: it shows which theme or plugin produced the markup. If PointStack Accessibility cannot fix it safely, use “Copy bug report” and send it to that theme or plugin’s author, or mark the issue as a false positive if you have checked it by hand.

Why are my results different from another checker?

Every tool tests a different set of rules and pages, and some run in a real browser while others read the HTML. PointStack Accessibility checks the pages your customers buy through, plus emails and PDFs. Differences are normal; the manual checklist covers what no automated tool can test.

Does it work with my page builder or cache plugin?

It reads the finished page, so it does not depend on how the page was built, and it stays out of the editing screens of Elementor, Divi, Bricks and other builders. When you change a fix it purges known caches (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache and others). If a page looks wrong, add it to Settings → Scanning → Skip output fixes on.

What does support cover?

PointStack Accessibility is self-service: you install, configure and run it yourself, and this FAQ, the screens and the Settings help text explain each step. Free version: the WordPress.org support forum. Paid plans: email support for bugs in the plugin and for questions the documentation does not answer. Support does not include setup calls, manual accessibility audits, reviewing your store, changes to your theme or other plugins, custom development or legal advice.

Does it slow my site down?

Most fixes are WordPress/WooCommerce filters with no measurable cost. The output pass (for markup no hook can reach) measured 5–10 ms per page on a standard WooCommerce store, less when a persistent object cache is available; you can switch it off or exclude URLs in Settings. Scans run only when you start them or after an update.

Does any data leave my site?

No. Scans, issues and fixes stay on your server. The only optional external calls are AI alt-text suggestions (sent only when you click “Suggest”, through the WordPress AI Client to the provider connected for your site) and, in Pro, the Slack/webhook alerts you configure.

My host blocks loopback requests

Server scans load your pages from your own server. If your host blocks that, the Overview shows the error; the browser check still works from your own browser.

What about microenterprises?

Businesses with fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover or balance sheet total up to €2 million are exempt from the EAA’s service requirements. PointStack Accessibility lets you record that declaration and reflects it in your statement — accessibility still helps your customers and sales.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Security: all generated markup is escaped at the point of output (wp_kses with an explicit allow-list, wp_kses_post for pagination); no escaping exceptions remain.
  • Documents (invoice, exemption record) print directly instead of echoing a built string.
  • The “Sort” button for product sorting now comes from a template served through WooCommerce’s template loader; WooCommerce template output is no longer buffered and re-printed.
  • Scan source tracing marks hook output without output buffering.
  • Form input is sanitised as it is read.
  • Readme: Freemius terms and privacy links, and what data it receives.
  • Fix: scans now work while WooCommerce’s “Coming soon” mode is on (only the plugin’s signed scan requests see the store; visitors still see the coming-soon page).
  • Fix: the Pro weekly email additions were lost when the email was built as separate text and HTML parts.

1.0.2

  • AI alt-text suggestions now use the WordPress AI Client and the provider connected in Settings → Connectors (WordPress 7.0+); the plugin no longer stores its own AI keys.
  • Page output fixes use the WordPress template output buffer (WordPress 6.9 or later is now required).
  • Scripts and styles on the printable documents are enqueued.

1.0.1

  • New installs show fixes to administrators only until you switch them on for everyone (Settings → Scanning → Who sees fixes).
  • A “not legal advice” notice next to the accessibility statement and the evidence pack, and in every evidence pack.
  • More answers in the FAQ: undoing fixes, issues caused by themes and other plugins, differences between checkers, page builders and caches, and what self-service support covers.

1.0.0

  • First release.
